text.p: Morgan Stockbroking Ltd said it was recomending magazine publisher Pacific Magazines & Printing Ltd as a buy for its dividend yield, strong cashflow, improving results and expansion strategies.

"Buy for attractive dividend yield, strong cashflow, improving results and long-term strategic gains from expansion into overseas markets and electronic delivery mediums," Morgan analyst Greg Cathro said in a report.
"There is a tinge of optimism about the 1996/97 outlook after a difficult previous year," Cathro said.
Further printing, distributioon and publishing opportunities will be explored in overseas regions to build on the good gains made in the Asian region in recent years, he said.

"The new division of CD manufacturing and video tape duplication will contribute to results during 1996/97 and offers the potential to service clients with electronic forms of media communication in the years ahead," Cathro said.
Cathro was forecasting net profits rising to A$72 million in the year ended June 30, 1997 from a reported $62 million in 1995/96.
"Overseas operations which were non-existent when the company floated in 1991, now represent 18 percent of sales revenue and 13 percent of earnings," Cathro said.
Meanwhile continued overseas expansion and the move into electronic comunications provided medium term opportunities which added to the reasonable short term outlook, Cathro said.
Pacific Magazines, 45 percent owned by News Corp Ltd, recently completed a takeover offer of multi-media Shomega Ltd.
